He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Memphis]]. ==College career== During both his sophomore and junior years on the team, the Tigers ended their season in the NCAA tournament's [[Elite Eight]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20080409220013/http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/apr/06/one-to-go---web-only-after-ucla-romp-tigers-eye/ One to go: After UCLA romp, Tigers eye Jayhawks] However, during his senior year Dorsey led the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]] to the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] championship game with [[Derrick Rose]] and [[Chris Douglas-Roberts]]. The Tigers fell to [[Kansas Jayhawks basketball|Kansas]] 75–68 in overtime. ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets=== Dorsey was chosen as the 33rd overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. After the draft, he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for the draft rights to the 25th pick, [[Nicolas Batum]]. In the [[2008–09 NBA season]], Dorsey played in 3 games, scoring a total of 2 points, grabbing one rebound, and making one assist. The Rockets assigned Dorsey to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4820575 Rockets call up Joey Dorsey from NBA Development League – ESPN] On February 5, 2010, after previously being called back up from the NBDL, Dorsey played a career-high 19 minutes and grabbed 12 rebounds.[http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/hotstories/6853966.html Dorsey gives Rockets a pick-me-up] ===Sacramento Kings / Toronto Raptors=== On February 18, 2010, Dorsey was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a three team deal that also moved the Rockets' [[Tracy McGrady]] to the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |title=KINGS: KINGS ACQUIRE CARL LANDRY, JOEY DORSEY AND LARRY HUGHES |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/trade_release_february.html |date=2010-02-18 |access-date=2010-02-19}} On March 28, 2010, he was waived by the Kings.{{cite web|title=Kings Waive Dorsey |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/joey_dorsey_release.html |date=2010-03-28 |access-date=2010-03-30 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100406065353/http://www.nba.com/kings/news/joey_dorsey_release.html |archive-date=April 6, 2010 }} On April 4, 2010, Dorsey was signed to a non-guaranteed contract by the [[Toronto Raptors|Raptors]].{{cite news|title=Raptors Sign Free Agent Joey Dorsey|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/dorseypr_040310.html|access-date=February 17, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2010}} ===Europe=== In September 2011, Dorsey signed a one-year deal with the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] club [[Saski Baskonia|Caja Laboral]].[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/87579/caja-laboral-lands-big-man-dorsey CAJA LABORAL lands big man Dorsey] On January 10, 2012, he parted ways with Caja Laboral.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/89707/caja-laboral-and-joey-dorsey-part-ways.html Caja Laboral and Joey Dorsey part ways] The next day, he signed with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/89717/olympiacos-signs-joey-dorsey.html Olympiacos signs Joey Dorsey] With Olympiacos, he won the [[Euroleague 2011–12|2011–12]] [[EuroLeague]] championship, as well as the 2011–12 Greek League championship. In August 2012, he re-signed with Olympiacos on a two-year deal.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/99077/olympiacos-re-signs-dorsey-through-2014 Olympiacos re-signs Dorsey through 2014] On September 12, 2012, during a preseason [[exhibition game]] against [[Dinamo Basket Sassari|Dinamo Sassari]], Dorsey ended up [[backboard shattering|shattering a backboard]], with around two minutes left in the fourth quarter.[https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/joey-dorsey-breaks-backboard-dunk-video-olympiacos-raptors-161958934--nba.html Ex-Rocket, King and Raptor Joey Dorsey shatters backboard with dunk during game for Greek team Olympiacos (VIDEO)] On November 7, 2012, Dorsey was released by Olympiacos, ending their relationship two weeks after he criticized the organization, and he stopped playing with the team.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/102565/180/olympiacos-officially-releases-dorsey Olympiacos officially releases Dorsey] On November 22, 2012, he signed with Turkish club [[Royal Halı Gaziantep]] for the rest of the [[2012–13 Turkish Basketball League]] season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/96772/joey-dorsey-signs-with-gaziantep-bsb.html Dorsey signs with Gaziantep BB] On July 17, 2013, Dorsey signed a one-year deal (with the option of a second) with the Spanish club [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]].{{cite web|title=FC Barcelona adds former Euroleague champ Joey Dorsey|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/103785/fc-barcelona-adds-former-euroleague-champ-joey-dorsey.html|work=Sportando.com|date=July 17, 2013|access-date=July 17, 2013 }} ===Return to the NBA=== On July 19, 2014, Dorsey signed with the Houston Rockets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-add-depth-roster-signings|title=Rockets Add Depth to Roster with Signings|work=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2014|access-date=July 20, 2015}} On January 21, 2015, he had a season-best game with seven points and 12 rebounds in a loss to the Golden State Warriors.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/dorsejo01/gamelog/2015/ Joey Dorsey 2014–15 Game Log] On July 20, 2015, the Rockets traded Dorsey, [[Nick Johnson (basketball)|Nick Johnson]], [[Kostas Papanikolaou]], [[Pablo Prigioni]], a 2016 first round draft pick, and cash considerations to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Ty Lawson]] and a 2017 second round draft pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-joey-dorsey-nick-johnson-kostas-papanikolaou-pablo-prigioni-cash-considerations|title=Nuggets Acquire Joey Dorsey, Nick Johnson, Kostas (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]].{{cite web|url=http://www.galatasaray.org/haber/basketbol/joey-dorsey-galatasaray-da/27675|title=Joey Dorsey Galatasaray'da|work=Galatasaray.org|date=August 29, 2017|language=es}} On February 13, 2017, Dorsey signed with [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]] club [[Best Balıkesir B.K.|Best Balıkesir]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 Turkish Basketball Super League|2016–17 BSL season]].{{cite news|title=Joey Dorsey signed with Best Balikesir|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/tbl/400823/joey-dorsey-signed-best-balikesir/|access-date=February 13, 2017|work=Eurohoops.net|date=February 13, 2017}} On November 2, 2018, Dorsey returned to [[Greek Basket League]] after six years, penning a deal with [[Panionios B.C.]] until the end of the [[2018–19 Greek Basket League|2018–19 season]]. Dorsey made 20 appearances and averaged 9 points and 8.8 rebounds in 22 minutes per game, helping Panionios to get some crucial victories in order to avoid relegation. On November 29, 2019, he has signed with [[Syntainics MBC]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/syntanics-mbc-ink-joey-dorsey/|title=Syntanics MBC ink Joey the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] announced the hiring of Joey Dorsey to serve as Player Development Assistant under head coach [[Chris Finch]].{{cite web |last1=Munz|first1=Jason|title=Timberwolves hire Appeal|access-date=February 12, 2025 |date=February 12, 2025}} He was then sent to be an Assistant Coach for the [[Iowa Wolves]] for the 2024-25 [[NBA G-League]] Season. ==Awards and accomplishments==
